supporting_observations.claim: At 13:44:40 UTC, Maria Lopez opened the macro-enabled document C:\Users\maria.lopez\Downloads\Statement.docm in Microsoft Word.

About six seconds later, Word launched PowerShell with hidden-window and no-profile options and an encoded command. The command decodes to an expression that downloads and executes a script from raw.githubusercontent.com/harbor-dental-it/tools/main/u.ps1.
The proxy recorded a successful request for that exact u.ps1 script, and the PowerShell process made the corresponding proxy connections.
The PowerShell process launched rundll32 to initialize C:\Users\maria.lopez\AppData\Roaming\svchelper.dll, a DLL path and execution pattern not explained by the supplied approved-software context.
The Word process exited shortly after launching PowerShell; PowerShell and rundll32 also exited within about 20 seconds of the initial PowerShell launch.
The reported 13:40 UTC time does not exactly match the observed suspicious chain, which begins at 13:44:40 UTC. The 13:40 records show an interactive logon sequence, not a PowerShell launch.

known_telemetry_limitations: The available records show the encoded PowerShell command and the successful script request, but do not include the contents of u.ps1.
The records show rundll32 invoking svchelper.dll but do not provide the DLL contents, signature, hash, or behavior after initialization.
The supplied window contains endpoint and network events but does not establish whether relevant activity occurred outside 13:20–14:20 UTC.
claims_not_established: Whether Maria intentionally opened the document or knew it would launch the observed commands.

Review network and authentication telemetry for follow-on connections, credential use, lateral movement, and possible data transfer associated with the host or these processes.
Confirm with Maria whether she opened Statement.docm and obtain the document's source and business context.
